caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.

The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of completions and coverage for four different models. The x-axis is labeled "Number of completions (k)" and uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 2^0 to 2^8, with tick labels at each power of 2. The y-axis is labeled "Coverage" and ranges from 0.2 to 0.9, with tick marks at 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. A blue solid line with circular markers represents "Llama-3B," starting at approximately 0.42 at k=1 and increasing to roughly 0.92 at k=256. A green dashed line with triangular markers represents "Llama-3B + FT," beginning at approximately 0.41 at k=1 and reaching approximately 0.92 at k=256. A light blue solid line with circular markers represents "Llama-1B," starting at approximately 0.22 at k=1 and increasing to approximately 0.72 at k=128. A light green dashed line with triangular markers represents "Llama-1B + FT," starting at approximately 0.27 at k=1 and increasing to approximately 0.77 at k=128.
